subject: history
topicDisplay: Migration to Britain c1000 to c2010
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: After the Norman Conquest of 1066, which ruler encouraged Jewish moneylenders to settle in England?
questions.explain: William I brought Jewish financiers from Normandy to provide the credit that the Church forbade Christians to offer.

questions.q: In which year did Edward I order the expulsion of all Jews from England?
questions.explain: Edward I expelled the Jewish community in 1290, and they were not officially readmitted until the 1650s.

questions.q: Why did Huguenots leave France in the late seventeenth century?
options: They were Protestants facing religious persecution
They were seeking gold in the New World
They had been defeated in a civil war
They were escaping the potato famine
questions.explain: As French Protestants, the Huguenots fled Catholic persecution, especially after the Edict of Nantes was revoked in 1685.

questions.q: Why did many Huguenot refugees settle in Spitalfields in London?
options: They established the area's silk-weaving industry
They worked in the local coal mines
questions.explain: Skilled Huguenot silk weavers made Spitalfields a centre of the luxury textile trade.

questions.q: Who permitted the readmission of Jews to England in 1656?
questions.explain: Cromwell allowed Jews to return, ending over 350 years of official exclusion.

questions.q: Why were Flemish weavers welcomed into medieval and early modern England?
options: They provided soldiers for the king's army
They could read and write Latin
questions.explain: Flemish weavers helped develop England's valuable woollen cloth industry.

questions.q: What was one consequence of Louis XIV revoking the Edict of Nantes in 1685?
options: Tens of thousands of Huguenots migrated to Britain
Lascars first arrived in British ports
questions.explain: The revocation removed Protestant legal protection in France, prompting mass Huguenot flight to Britain and elsewhere.

questions.q: In which year did the Irish potato famine that caused mass migration begin?
questions.explain: The Great Famine began in 1845 when potato blight destroyed the crop, driving many Irish people to migrate to British cities.

questions.q: A nineteenth-century record shows large numbers of Irish-born men working on canal and railway construction. What does this best illustrate?
options: Irish migrants often took hard labouring work as 'navvies'
Irish migrants were mostly silk weavers
Irish migrants usually worked as ships' officers
questions.explain: Many Irish migrants found employment as navvies building Britain's canals and railways.

questions.q: Jewish migrants who fled pogroms in the 1880s came mainly from which empire?
questions.explain: Violent pogroms in the Russian Empire after 1881 drove many Jews to seek refuge in Britain.

questions.q: Why was the Aliens Act of 1905 introduced?
options: To restrict immigration, especially of poor Jewish refugees
To give Commonwealth citizens British passports
To recruit workers from the Caribbean
questions.explain: The 1905 Aliens Act was Britain's first major law limiting immigration, driven partly by hostility towards Eastern European Jewish arrivals.

questions.q: Who were the Lascars in this period?
options: Sailors from South Asia employed on British ships
questions.explain: Lascars were South Asian seamen who worked on British merchant and naval vessels, some settling in port cities.

questions.q: Why did many Eastern European Jewish migrants settle in the East End of London?
options: Cheap housing, an existing Jewish community and work in the clothing trade
Free land offered by the government
questions.explain: The East End offered affordable housing, a supportive community and 'sweated' tailoring work needing little English.

questions.q: A historian notes that many newly arrived Jewish immigrants worked long hours in small tailoring workshops. Which conclusion is best supported?
options: The clothing trade offered work that required little English or capital
Immigrants were banned from all other jobs by law
Most immigrants were wealthy factory owners
Tailoring was the only industry in Britain
questions.explain: 'Sweated' tailoring provided accessible employment for newcomers with few resources or English-language skills.

questions.q: Which ship brought a well-known group of Caribbean migrants to Tilbury in 1948?
questions.explain: The Empire Windrush arrived at Tilbury in June 1948, symbolising post-war Caribbean migration to Britain.

questions.q: What did the British Nationality Act of 1948 allow?
options: Commonwealth citizens to live and work in Britain
Only Europeans to settle in Britain
An immediate end to all immigration
questions.explain: The 1948 Act confirmed Commonwealth citizens' right to settle in Britain, encouraging post-war migration.

questions.q: In 1972, which leader expelled Asians from Uganda, many of whom migrated to Britain?
questions.explain: Idi Amin expelled Uganda's Asian population in 1972, and many, holding British passports, came to Britain.

questions.q: In 1961 a Jamaican citizen could freely settle in Britain, but a year later faced new restrictions. Which law caused this change?
questions.explain: The 1962 Act introduced controls on Commonwealth immigration, limiting entry through a voucher system.

questions.q: Why was the Notting Hill Carnival established in the 1960s?
options: To celebrate Caribbean culture and improve community relations
To mark the end of the Second World War
questions.explain: The Carnival grew as a celebration of Caribbean heritage, helping ease tensions after unrest such as the 1958 disturbances.

questions.q: After the European Union expanded in 2004, Britain experienced a notable increase in migrants from which region?
options: Central and Eastern Europe, especially Poland
questions.explain: The 2004 EU enlargement, admitting countries such as Poland, led to significant Eastern European migration to Britain.
